summary: Kegelman Air Force Auxiliary Field is a small military airfield located near Cherokee, Oklahoma, serving as a satellite training facility for Vance Air Force Base in nearby Enid. Originally established during World War II, it remains an active auxiliary field used primarily for pilot training operations, including touch-and-go practice and emergency procedures. The field supports Undergraduate Pilot Training (UPT) programs and contributes to the region's long aviation heritage.
faqs:
Q: What is Kegelman AF Aux Field used for?
A: It functions primarily as an auxiliary training airfield for Vance Air Force Base, supporting pilot training operations such as touch-and-go landings and low-level approaches.

Q: Is Kegelman open to civilian pilots?
A: As an active military auxiliary field, it is generally restricted to military and authorized aircraft only. Civilian pilots should verify status through NOTAMs and official channels before attempting to land.

Q: Which major base is it associated with?
A: Kegelman is a satellite facility of Vance Air Force Base, located approximately 30 miles southeast in Enid, Oklahoma.

Q: When was Kegelman established?
A: The field dates back to the World War II era and has been in continuous use for military aviation training since its founding.
transport_tips: The airfield is located in a rural area of Alfalfa County, so personal or rental vehicles are typically needed for ground transportation. The nearest major commercial airport is Will Rogers World Airport in Oklahoma City, roughly two hours southeast. Visitors should coordinate access through Vance AFB security protocols well in advance, as the facility is on military-controlled land.
local_tip: If you're visiting the area, take time to explore the Cherokee Strip Museum in nearby Cherokee to learn about the historic 1893 land run that shaped this part of Oklahoma, giving you a deeper sense of the region's pioneer and aviation heritage.
